s:
One of the Reason(s) for Agricultural distress in India is

a. Failure of Land Reforms

b. Limited use of new Agricultural technology

c. Adoption of cropping pattern

d. More Financial Assistance by Union and State Governments
Correct Answer
x: Failure of land reforms and limited use of new agricultural technology are reasons for farm distress; more government assistance is not.

s: What was the primary aim of land reforms in India?
x: The primary aim of land reforms was equitable distribution of land ownership (land to the tiller); tenancy stabilisation, consolidation and secure titles were means to it.

s: Land reforms in Andhra Pradesh aimed at implementing the land ceiling and changing the size of land holdings for
x: The APPSC key says AP's ceiling laws and changes in holding size aimed at productive utilisation of land.

s: With reference to land reforms in independent India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The ceiling laws were aimed at family holdings and not individual holdings.
The major aim of land reforms was providing agricultural land to all the landless.
It resulted in cultivation of cash crops as a predominant form of cultivation.
Land reforms permitted no exemptions to the ceiling limits.
x: The UPSC 2019 key: the major aim was providing agricultural land to the landless. Ceilings were first on individual holdings, exemptions (plantations, orchards) were allowed and cash crops did not become predominant.

s: Which one of the followings is not a part of land reforms in India?
x: Abolition of zamindari, ceiling on holdings and tenancy reform are land reforms; a multiple-cropping scheme is not.

s: Which of the following measures have been taken to make the agrarian structure conducive to agricultural growth?
x: Abolition of intermediaries, tenancy reforms and ceiling on holdings were all used to make the agrarian structure conducive to growth.

s: Legally stipulated maximum size beyond which no individual farmer can hold any land is :
x: Land ceiling is the legal maximum an individual or family may hold; the surplus goes to the landless.

s: Land distributed to the poor and other weaker sections is
o: much higher in the distribution of ceilings surplus land
much higher than government lands assignments
forest lands share is much higher
x: In AP land distributed to the poor came overwhelmingly from government (assigned) land, so it is not 'much higher' from ceiling surplus (a) or forest land (c), and (b) reverses the fact – none of them.

x: Indira Prabha (2004, YSR) developed uncultivable barren assigned lands allotted to landless poor farmers.
